release-beta-cut-071.choice: A manual Cut beta workflow, run by Ronald or an agent with his go, publishes x.y.z-beta.N from current main under the plugin's separate -beta Registry package. x.y.z is the version the pending changesets would release; N is one more than the highest beta tag or Registry beta version. release-beta-cut-071.question: How are betas cut and final releases gated, the same way for every DinkusKit Registry plugin?
release-beta-cut-071.rationale: The Registry has no channels, so only a separate -beta package keeps betas off real stores. A cut-on-demand beta, as OpenClaw cuts betas from a chosen commit, removes the pre-mode enter and exit PRs and a review per beta, and betas exist only when someone is ready to test one. The journeys run on a set-up machine, not in GitHub Actions, so a recorded pass is the gate. Identical files keep the release path the same across plugins. Payments first needs its beta installed ID accepted by Payments and DinkusKit.com, its v0.2.8 baseline tag, and a Payments setup journey. Sequence: Commerce finishes 0.3.0 in pre mode, then both repos switch after go-live.

Owners and Administrators may always print. A plain employee may print once the owner ticks Print shipping labels in Ship (ship:labels). A refresh is refused once the person signs out of DinkusKit.com, their email changes, they are removed or suspended or lose the permission, the business is suspended or unapproved, the operator cuts Ship off, the owner turns Ship off, or an old refresh token comes back. A refresh extends the DinkusKit.com sign-in the way a visit would. The pass carries no store name or reply-to: Commerce sends the EmDash Site title with each order, and Ship keeps its own reply-to setting.
